ana: quick sync — ran a classifier->kernel handoff probe on EU pool. goal: cut kernel-switch overhead for short, fast-decode prompts. baseline (no classifier) p50=42ms p95=320ms. classifier+handoff p50=38ms p95=210ms. notes below.

sam: nice. how are you mapping decode_rate buckets to kernel choices? any churn from KV cache warmups?

devin: mapping used in probe: decode_rate <5 tok/s -> kernel-A (low-mem slower matmul), 5-20 -> kernel-B (vectorized), >20 -> kernel-C (fused/faster). prompt_len buckets were <64, 64-256, >256. quick snippet we ran: 
```
# classifier rules (simplified)
if prompt_len < 64 and est_decode_rate > 20:
    kernel = 'C'
elif prompt_len < 64:
    kernel = 'B'
elif prompt_len < 256:
    kernel = 'B'
else:
    kernel = 'A'
```
This kept most small fast decodes on C, long contexts on A.

ryan: profiling: kernel handoff cost = cold switch ~14ms (init + JNI), warm switch ~3-5ms. KV cache priming matters: if we predict kernel correctly and prime the KV layout, subsequent requests save ~10-12ms each.

maya: did you test token-budget targeting as part of batching? e.g., let short reqs wait to fill budget 64/128 before dispatch.

ana: (typo) ana: yes — ran token-budget sweep. budget=64 reduced p95 tail for bursty short requests but increased avg latency for interactive sessions by ~2-3ms. config used for the canary: `--token-budget=64 --queue-delay-ms=6`. overall tradeoff favorable for throughput-first routes.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-02-22T13:05:01Z: perf-probe/classifier-kernel-handoff -> rolled to eu-pool v12 :white_check_mark:

sam: any regressions? OOMs? higher GC?

devin: one regression observed in mixed-length sessions (~200 tokens): kernel-A chosen initially (smaller memory path) then switched to kernel-C for decode rate => KV layout mismatch caused extra evictions and small thrash. root cause: kernel-A and kernel-C use different in-memory KV layout IDs. workaround: prefer kernels that preserve `kv_layout_id` for multi-request sessions. patch proposed in PR #4421 to add layout preference.

ana: ana: good catch. next steps: (1) add soft constraint to classifier to prefer same-KV-layout kernels for sessions with >1 req; (2) automate token-budget per route via route_config; (3) run 24h canary with user-sim09 and collect `kernel_choice` + `kv_layout_id` logs. I'll open tickets and link dashboards.

ryan: +1. also recommend we log `kernel_choice`, `kv_layout_id`, `est_decode_rate`, and `token_budget` per request (7d retention) so we can correlate tail events.

maya: also check kernel cold-starts overlap with autoscaler spin-up; that 14ms cold switch stacks badly if a pod is booting. maybe pre-warm preferred kernels on scale-up.

ana: ana: agreed — add prewarm hint when autoscaler detects new instance for high-throughput routes.

sam: can we get a small dashboard: p50/p95 by (prompt_len_bucket, decode_rate_bucket, kernel_choice)? would make it easy to spot regressions.

devin: will add a dashboard panel. will tag metrics as `prompt_bucket`, `decode_bucket`, `kernel`.

ana: thanks all — i'll file the tickets (classifier layout preference, token-budget automation, logging retention) and post the canary link.

ryan: thanks.

maya: 👍

ana: closing for now, will follow up with numbers + dashboard link.
